// Exponential backoff with jitter, the way a client that must be polite to
// a struggling server does it: capped delay, bounded retries, full jitter.

import java.time.Duration;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.concurrent.ThreadLocalRandom;

public final class Retry {
    private static final Duration BASE = Duration.ofMillis(250);
    private static final Duration CAP = Duration.ofSeconds(8);
    private static final int MAX_ATTEMPTS = 5;

    /* delayFor is the backoff curve: base doubled per attempt, capped. */
    private static Duration delayFor(int attempt) {
        long doubled = BASE.toMillis() << (attempt - 1);
        long capped = Math.min(doubled, CAP.toMillis());
        return Duration.ofMillis(capped);
    }

    public static <T> T call(List<String> hosts, Operation<T> op)
            throws InterruptedException {
        for (int attempt = 1; attempt <= MAX_ATTEMPTS; attempt++) {
            for (String host : hosts) {
                try {
                    return op.run(host);
                } catch (TransientError error) {
                    System.err.println("attempt " + attempt + " on " + host
                            + " failed: " + error.getMessage());
                }
            }
            long jitter = ThreadLocalRandom.current().nextLong(0, 2);
            Duration wait = delayFor(attempt).plusMillis(jitter);
            Thread.sleep(wait.toMillis());
        }
        throw new IllegalStateException("all attempts exhausted");
    }

    interface Operation<T> {
        T run(String host) throws TransientError;
    }

    static class TransientError extends Exception {
        TransientError(String message) {
            super(message);
        }
    }
}
